newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end choppy trading mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end choppy trading mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended a session of choppy trading mixed, with Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures keeping tiny gains after noncommittal trade.
September S&P 500s popped up again briefly after U.S. Treasury bond futures closed, hitting a fresh session peak at 921.00 as a dealer bought and forced locals to cover shorts, brokers said.
The contract hit some buy stops above the day's previous peak at 919.50 during the technically inspired advance but lacked power to follow through on the upside and soon faded back toward unchanged.
Traders also said nervousness ahead of IBM second-quarter earnings, which were reported after the close at $1.46 per share, as well as Tuesday's start of Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, kept players shy.
"There was not much," said one S&P 500 futures broker of afternoon trade. "It was pretty much as expected, a range-trade waiting for Greenspan."

Early weakness stemmed from softening in U.S. Treasury bond futures, plus carryover pressure from Friday's selloff that left futures hanging on to a very tight premium over cash that drew some arbitrage sell programs early.

Fair value Monday was roughly 6.00 points, using the London Interbank Offered Rate. Arbitrage buy programs would have needed about 6.80 points over cash, while sell programs required about 5.20 points premium.
September S&P 500s held support at the overnight low of 911.25 but also stayed shy of good resistance at 922.95.

Sept S&P 500s ended up 0.75 pt at 917.75, Value Lines lost 1.70 to 815.00, Nikkei rose 130.0 to 20,350.0., Midcaps fell 1.75 to 302.65, NYSE Composite firmed 0.35 to 477.50, Russell 2000 fell 2.25 to 406.25, and NASDAQ 100 dropped 15.75 to 1,065.00.
